title: Picatrix Fragment, Steganographia, Paracelsus & Chemical Secrets
shelf_note: The catalogue calls this a Latin occult/chemical miscellany (Picatrix, Trithemius, Paracelsus). This leaf is a German Protestant devotional or polemical text (Nicodemus, Christ's flesh and blood, false prophets who 'bring his body down into the bread'). It may be one item in a composite codex (the banner shows Vat. Reg.lat.1344), but neither the title nor language=Latin describes it. The collections metadata is empty.
rights_flag: The licence stamp is part of the scan: a footer reads "Copyright © Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana / https://digi.vatlib.it/view/MSS_Reg.lat.1344/0123 / powered by AMLAD·NTT DATA", and a diagonal watermark reads "Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana ... ALL RIGHTS RESERVED ©". The manuscript is early modern. The digital image is a Vatican Library copyright reproduction.
structure_note: There are 314 records, all with OCR. structure.pages_translated is 0 but the book field says 272, so the two counts disagree. 155 pages carry a printed number, with 44 backsteps and 34 repeats. In a composite manuscript, that fits separately foliated items bound together, plus misread hand numerals. It is probably not a scan splice, but I cannot confirm that from one leaf. This leaf's '60' matches the OCR <page-num>.

pages.layout: single column of German cursive inside a ruled frame. The facing leaf's edge and a few line-ends show at the left. There is a short mark or catchword below the bottom rule at the right. Vatican copyright banner and watermark.

ocr_errors.ocr:
Die ursachin diser Gebur wast wundertlichwol das
verstehn.
ocr_errors.image: Si Celestia dixero Vobis, wast wundert ihr wol dabo / verstehn
ocr_errors.problem: The image has a Latin quotation from John 3:12 ('Si coelestia dixero vobis', 'if I tell you of heavenly things'). The OCR replaces it with an invented German clause about 'the cause of this birth'.

ocr_errors.ocr: Wer so in Christo Christus, und wir in ihm
ocr_errors.image: Aber so in uns Christus, und wir in ihm
ocr_errors.problem: 'in uns' ('in us') is misread as 'in Christo', and 'Aber' as 'Wer'. The translation recovers the sense ('If Christ is in us').

ocr_errors.ocr: Wer in Christo und wir in ihm,
ocr_errors.image: Aber in uns, und wir in ihm,
ocr_errors.problem: The same misread again. This time it carries into the English as 'If he is in Christ'.
'Erd' ('earth') is misread as 'dar', so 'his Word on earth' is lost.
'Creatur' is normalised to 'Natur', which loses the Pauline 'new creature' (2 Cor 5:17).

ocr_errors.ocr: Und Jesas ihn beweist d. Mitteller
ocr_errors.image: Dan(d) Ich hab ihn versp(e)rt(?) d Mittel(e)r
ocr_errors.problem: Hard to read, but the image does not show 'Jesas … beweist'. The translation then names Jesus as the subject.

ocr_errors.image: a large display word, possibly 'Martes' or a gospel attribution such as 'Marcus'; illegible to me
ocr_errors.problem: The OCR gives a reading that makes no sense, with no <unclear> marker.
'können' ('can') is misread as 'kommen'. The translation's 'by our own power' covers it.

tr_errors.source:
Die ursachin diser Gebur wast wundertlichwol das
verstehn.
tr_errors.english: The cause of this birth was a wondrous thing to understand.
tr_errors.problem: This faithfully translates the invented OCR clause. The leaf has the Latin John 3:12 quotation ('If I have told you heavenly things…'), so the reader gets a sentence that is not on the page.

tr_errors.source: Wer in Christo und wir in ihm,
tr_errors.english: If he is in Christ and we in him,
tr_errors.problem: Carries the misread forward. The image says 'if [Christ is] in us and we in him'.

tr_errors.source:
Also haben wir sein Worttauff
dar.
tr_errors.english: Thus we have his Word on it: there is Christ also.
tr_errors.problem: The image reads 'his Word on earth, there is Christ also'. The English turns this into an idiom ('his Word on it').

tr_errors.source: Und Jesas ihn beweist d. Mitteller
tr_errors.english: And Jesus shows him that the Mediator
tr_errors.problem: 'Jesus' is supplied from the misread 'Jesas'. The image does not seem to name Jesus here.

tr_errors.source: Wie die in d. Rauch gebeist gleichwol muge sag:
tr_errors.english: Just as those who are steeped in the smoke may nonetheless say:
tr_errors.problem: Confident English over an uncertain reading, with no uncertainty marker. The image line looks closer to 'in d Steinen gebruckt'. I read it with low confidence.

missing.english: Bartos/ At that same time, he says, false prophets will arise.
missing.why: 'Bartos' is left as an unexplained word. A reader cannot tell whether it is a speaker, a source attribution or a gospel reference (Matt 24 / Mark 13).

missing.english: Was the Lord right, then, to keep silent at such Pharisaic questioning by Nicodemus?
missing.why: The passage depends on John 3 (Nicodemus and the new birth from above). A short note would anchor the argument that follows.

missing.english: Just as those who are steeped in the smoke may nonetheless say: there is Christ.
missing.why: The sentence makes no sense as English. The reader needs to know that the reading is uncertain or what it alludes to.

missing.english: who with earthly arts such as logic and rhetoric will try to master Christ in his sacraments
missing.why: This is the Reformation-era Eucharist controversy (bread and body). The polemical target is not explained.

book_verdict: The leaf matches its OCR and the folio '60' matches. But a Latin John 3:12 quotation is replaced by an invented German clause, which is translated as a sentence the page does not contain, and several other cursive misreads carry into the English. The page is a German theological text under a Latin occult-miscellany title, and the scan has a Vatican copyright banner burned in.
